---
title: "masbayes: Bayesian Genomic Prediction Models for SNPs and Microhaplotypes"
---

## masbayes: Bayesian Genomic Prediction Models for SNPs and Microhaplotypes {.unnumbered}


### Description

Bayesian methods for genomic prediction using SNP or microhaplotype
markers. Implements BayesR (four-class mixture) and
BayesA (marker-specific variance), each available as full MCMC or
stochastic EM. Continuous (Gaussian) and binary (Albert-Chib data
augmentation) traits are supported.



### Workflow

The standard pipeline is three steps:


<ol>
<li> <code>construct_wah_matrix()</code> — build the
$W_{\alpha h}$ design matrix from phased haplotypes.

</li>
<li> <code>run_bayesr()</code> or <code>run_bayesa()</code> — fit
the Bayesian model. The fit object is auto-saved to
<code>results_bayesr.Rds</code> / <code>results_bayesa.Rds</code> by default.

</li>
<li> <code>summary(fit)</code> — full report (heritability, MCMC ESS /
Geweke, variance components, training metrics, top alleles).

</li>
<li> <code>predict(fit, newdata, y_new)</code> — evaluate the model on
any data: in-sample, test split, or k-fold CV held-out fold.

</li></ol>



### Three usage scenarios

<code>summary()</code> and <code>predict()</code> are scheme-agnostic — the same
methods cover all three of:


<ul>
<li> <strong>Full-data fit:</strong> train on everything;
<code>predict(fit)</code> returns in-sample metrics.

</li>
<li> <strong>Train/test split:</strong> train on a subset; evaluate via
<code>predict(fit, W_test, y_test)</code>.

</li>
<li> <strong>k-fold CV:</strong> the user loops over folds (typically with
<code>save_rds = FALSE</code>, <code>verbose = FALSE</code>), then
<code>predict()</code> on each held-out fold.

</li></ul>

Cross-validation orchestration is intentionally left to the caller —
the package does not ship a built-in <code>cv_*()</code> helper.



### Quick start

<pre>
library(masbayes)

# 1. Design matrix
train &lt;- construct_wah_matrix(hap, colnames(hap), allele_freq)
W     &lt;- train\$W_ah

# 2. Sufficient statistics
wtw &lt;- colSums(W^2)

# 3. Fit
fit &lt;- run_bayesr(W, y, wtw,
                  sigma2_e_init = var(y) * 0.5,
                  sigma2_ah     = var(y) * 0.5,
                  method        = "mcmc")

# 4. Report and evaluate
summary(fit)
pred &lt;- predict(fit, W_test, y_test)   # train/test mode
pred\$metrics\$accuracy
</pre>


### Main functions


<dl>
<dt><code>construct_wah_matrix</code></dt><dd>Build the
$W_{\alpha h}$ design matrix.
</dd>
<dt><code>run_bayesr</code></dt><dd>Fit BayesR (4-class mixture).
</dd>
<dt><code>run_bayesa</code></dt><dd>Fit BayesA (marker-specific
variance).
</dd>
<dt><code>summary.masbayes_bayesr</code>,
<code>summary.masbayes_bayesa</code></dt><dd>Full-fit reports
(S3 methods).
</dd>
<dt><code>predict.masbayes_bayesr</code>,
<code>predict.masbayes_bayesa</code></dt><dd>GEBV + metrics, scheme-
agnostic (S3 methods).
</dd>
</dl>



### Output of run_bayesr() / run_bayesa()

The returned S3 object (class <code>masbayes_bayesr</code> or
<code>masbayes_bayesa</code>) contains:


<ul>
<li> <code>GEBV</code>, <code>beta_hat</code>, <code>beta_samples</code> (and
<code>sigma2_j_samples</code> for BayesA)

</li>
<li> <code>sigma2_e_samples</code>, <code>mu_samples</code>, <code>runtime</code>
(seconds)

</li>
<li> <code>h2</code>, <code>sigma2_g</code>, <code>sigma2_e</code>

</li>
<li> <code>training_metrics</code>: <code>R2</code>, <code>RMSE</code>,
<code>accuracy</code>/<code>AUC</code>, <code>bias</code>

</li>
<li> <code>diagnostics</code>: ESS, Geweke Z (MCMC only)

</li>
<li> <code>variance_components</code>: small / medium / large + <code>pi</code>
(BayesR), or tertile bins of marker variances (BayesA)

</li>
<li> <code>rds_path</code>: where the fit was auto-saved

</li></ul>

Disable auto-save with <code>save_rds = FALSE</code> — recommended for CV
loops.



### Low-level bindings

<code>run_bayesr_mcmc()</code>, <code>run_bayesr_em()</code>,
<code>run_bayesa_mcmc()</code>, and <code>run_bayesa_em()</code> are the direct
Rust bindings. They are exported but undocumented; prefer
<code>run_bayesr()</code> / <code>run_bayesa()</code> for routine use.
